description: Open Quartz is Open Climate Fix's open solar-generation forecast for individual photovoltaic sites. A Python interface accepts latitude, longitude, installed capacity and forecast time, combines them with numerical weather predictions, and returns generation in kilowatts over a zero-to-48-hour horizon. Scripts can collect forecasts in CSV, and a separately hosted API is documented. Geographic coverage of the interface is broad, but the models were trained on UK sites; application elsewhere requires caution. Public software is free under MIT, distinct from the provider's commercial forecast. A limitation is the mismatch between the training weather source and supported GFS, ICON or ECMWF inputs. Historical requests also face missing variables and model-specific time restrictions. The README describes usage logging with an opt-out setting. The package can provide solar scenarios for dispatch and storage studies with PyPSA (model-pypsa). The public repository identifies a software DOI. No service request containing a real site, dataset download or accuracy benchmark was performed.
name: Open Quartz solar forecast
